title: SerialBot: AI serial port assistant and MCP server for UART
description: Open-source serial port assistant for Windows, macOS and Linux with a built-in MCP server: AI agents read UART logs and test ESP32/STM32 boards.
hero_title: The verification loop for embedded hardware.
hero_lede: Coding agents earn trust by checking their own work. On a board, checking means watching what the firmware does, and that comes out of the serial port. SerialBot hands the agent that port: it flashes, reads the log and verifies on its own, and you approve every change.
uart_title: UART waveform of the command AT+GMR followed by CR LF, 8N1
uart_caption: AT+GMR\r\n on the wire: start bit, eight data bits from the least significant, stop bit. This is what SerialBot passes to the agent, and nothing else.
loop_title: Closing the loop on the bench
loop_intro: With the serial port in reach, the agent goes around the loop itself instead of waiting for you to paste the log back.
loop_steps: Flash. The agent hands the port to your flashing tool and takes it back afterwards. The log keeps going.
Read the log. It waits for the line it expects, or notices the timeout.
Change the code. It adds the prints it needs, or the fix.
Build and flash again. Round the loop until the log says it works.
loop_note: You stay in charge: every change the agent wants to make to a port is shown to you first, and every line it sent is tagged AI in the window.

features.Connect: Many ports at once (each can have a window of its own; closing one keeps its log), TCP client, TCP server with several clients, UDP, auto-reconnect after replugging.
features.Receive: Text or HEX with millisecond timestamps, ANSI colors, GBK and other encodings, frame gaps, search and filter, keyword highlight, line numbers and bookmarks.
features.Terminal mode: A full terminal emulator on any session: log in to a Linux board, run top or vi.
features.Plot: Numbers in received lines, such as temp=23.6 hum=41 or 1.2, 3.4, drawn as live curves.
features.Send: Multi-line text or HEX, checksums (CRC-8/16/32, XOR, SUM, LRC), timed send, command lists (also in a window of their own), files.
features.Signals: DTR and RTS switches, line lamps, BREAK, timed sequences such as a reset pulse.
features.Small: About 4.5 MB to install on Windows, or a single portable exe. Linux x64 and arm64, macOS universal.

shot_terminal: An agent's commands tagged AI next to your own, with line numbers, Δt, a bookmark and the command list.
shot_windows: Several ports side by side: esp32 in a window of its own next to the main window.
shot_plot: Sensor values from the log drawn live, each curve on its own scale.
shot_tty: Terminal mode: vim running on a board's shell, keys sent straight to the device.

verify_title: Agents you can trust check their own work
verify_body:
The teams getting the most out of coding agents treat verification as the core of the work, not an afterthought. Lauren Tan (@poteto), who builds Grok Bot, describes letting agents run the app, take traces and test it the way a user would, and keep going until it really works. Closing that loop is what makes their pull requests trustworthy.

Firmware has had no such loop. The truth about embedded code is on the board, and the board speaks through its serial port, so a person has had to watch the terminal and relay what it said. SerialBot is the missing piece: it lets the agent run the board and read the answer itself.
cli_intro: serialbot-cli is SerialBot without a window, a separate download: one-shot commands for scripts and CI, an interactive terminal with minicom's keys, a full-screen view of several ports with a waveform and the AI panel, scripts, and the same MCP server.
cli_then: serialbot-cli mcp serve runs the MCP server on its own and asks about an agent's changes in the terminal; serialbot-cli completions bash|zsh|fish|powershell prints completions.
privacy_intro: SerialBot collects no personal data: everything it receives and keeps stays on your computer.
privacy_body:
What SerialBot does not do

SerialBot (the desktop app and serialbot-cli) has no account, no analytics, no telemetry, no ads and no crash reporting. It does not send what you receive or type to us or to anyone else, and we cannot see how you use it.

What stays on your computer

The data you send and receive, the logs, command lists, history and settings (including the MCP server's token) are kept on your computer, in the app's data folder. Logs are written to a file only when you save or capture them, to the place you choose. Removing the app, or that folder, removes them.

Network connections

SerialBot connects only where you tell it to: the TCP and UDP addresses you open. Its MCP server listens on this computer only (127.0.0.1) unless you choose to open it to your local network; clients need its token either way.

AI agents

SerialBot does not talk to any AI service itself. When you connect an AI agent (for example Claude Desktop or Claude Code) to its MCP server and let it use a session, what the agent reads from the port goes to that agent, and through it to the AI provider you use, under that provider's privacy policy. Actions that change a device wait for your approval unless you allow them, and you can switch the server off at any time.

Downloads and this website

This website sets no cookies and uses no analytics; its fonts are served from this site. The download section asks GitHub for the latest release from your browser. The site is hosted on GitHub Pages, and the app is distributed through GitHub and the Microsoft Store; GitHub's and Microsoft's own privacy statements apply to those services.

Children

SerialBot collects no personal data from anyone, including children.

Changes and contact

If this policy changes, the new version is published on this page with its date. Questions: Jerry, support@aiany.cc or strongwong003@gmail.com.
